title: Corpus Juris Civilis
summary: The Corpus Juris Civilis, Emperor Justinian I's compilation of Roman law, was prepared in Constantinople under his minister Tribonian. It consisted of the Codex, issued in 529, the Digest, completed by the end of 533, and the Institutes, an introductory textbook. It became highly influential for European legal culture.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia's Justinian page gives the completed corpus as between 529 and 534 CE; start here is the Codex (529), end the Digest (533).

as_recorded.value: The first part of the Corpus Juris Civilis was completed in April 529 CE
the Digest (or Pandects), issued in December 533 CE
The Digest was completed by the end of AD 533

where.historical_name: Constantinople, capital of the East Roman Empire

importance.justification: Max-EuP 2012 calls it the most influential document for European legal culture.

sources.title: Corpus Juris Civilis

reviewer_note: The World History Encyclopedia corpus page is loose on dates (says two more parts followed "the following year" after April 529); the summary relies on the Max-EuP date for the Digest and the WHE April 529 and December 533 statements.
